summary: Feed s139_double to IDS is degraded: 6.5% TCP packet loss and severe tool overload (3.34 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port, 334% capacity). Loss correlates with overload bursts causing broker/egress drops. IDS will miss attacks due to incomplete flows.

findings.root_cause: 122 of 1880 TCP packets (6.49%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating buffer drops. Correlates directly with 3.34 Gbps bursts exceeding the 1 Gbps IDS port - packet broker egress queues overflow and tail-drop under sustained overload, not random link errors.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams or perform full payload inspection (required by profile). Results in missed signatures, broken flow state, false negatives and evasion opportunity for attackers.

recommended_fix.why: Scale egress capacity to eliminate drops. Distributing flows 5-tuple hashed across 3-4x 1Gbps IDS ports keeps per-port rate <80% and preserves both directions and full payload required by IDS.

findings.root_cause: Peak burst 3.34 Gbps in 1ms vs 1 Gbps IDS port (334% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals). Aggregation of multiple source links to single 1G tool port without load balancing. SPAN/broker is oversubscribed.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC discards excess traffic indiscriminately. Even if broker forwards, tool cannot process line rate - detection engine drops packets, loses visibility during bursts when attacks are most likely to be hidden.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs both directions and full payload, so slicing/filtering would hurt coverage. Load balancing across a 4-port IDS cluster or 4x 1G tool ports with flow-aware hashing keeps each port under 0.8 Gbps threshold while retaining complete sessions.
